name: Free accredited veterans claims help
description: Accredited TVC benefits advisors provide claims assistance at no charge.
next_step: Give your county and ask to arrange help with a VA claim, appeal, pension or survivor benefit.
constraints: Ask what records to bring. A referral does not determine benefit eligibility or a claim outcome.

name: Texas State Veterans Homes
organization: Texas Veterans Land Board / General Land Office
description: State veterans homes offer long-term care for qualified veterans, spouses and Gold Star parents.
next_step: Ask the Veterans Land Board about home locations, admissions review, care needs and payment arrangements.
constraints: Admission and care requirements apply. Confirm current availability and payer arrangements with admissions.

fields_supported: Veterans Land Board statewide public phone

name: Texas Aging and Disability Resource Centers
description: Statewide starting line for aging, disability and long-term support referrals.
next_step: Give your county and describe the support needed; ask to connect with the appropriate ADRC or local program.
constraints: Each referred program reviews its own eligibility and availability.

name: Texas Area Agencies on Aging directory
description: Official directory of 28 aging agencies and their published county service areas.
next_step: Ask for the aging agency serving your county and the services available for the person needing support.
constraints: County mapping is in the regional records; LaSalle needs a supplemental official regional-council source.

fields_supported: statewide AAA phone and services for older adults and caregivers

name: Texas Health Information, Counseling and Advocacy Program
organization: Texas HICAP / Health and Human Services
description: Texas’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program provides Medicare insurance counseling.
next_step: Ask for a benefits counselor to review Medicare choices, coverage questions or help paying costs.
constraints: Confirm the counseling process and any assistance-program requirements. No enrollment outcome is promised.

fields_supported: free unbiased HICAP Medicare counseling and statewide line

name: STAR+PLUS home and community services screening
description: STAR+PLUS HCBS offers long-term support services, with home adaptations subject to the member’s service plan.
next_step: Existing STAR+PLUS members: ask the health plan’s service coordinator about HCBS assessment. Other applicants: ask the ADRC about screening and the appropriate application or interest-list route.
constraints: Program-specific financial and care criteria apply. Medicaid enrollment alone does not establish HCBS or home modification coverage.
Ask the MCO service coordinator about documented need, service-plan authorization, vendor requirements and written owner permission before arranging work.

fields_supported: STAR+PLUS HCBS minor home modification service
source_evidence.published_or_revised_on: Section 6600 effective 2018-09-03; sections 6610 and 6640 effective 2016-03-01; other subsections have later revision dates

fields_supported: ADRC statewide long-term support navigation phone
STAR+PLUS service coordination and HCBS screening scope

name: Texas State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
organization: Texas Health and Human Services / State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
description: Statewide navigation for resident advocacy in nursing and assisted living facilities.
next_step: Give the facility name and county; ask for the appropriate long-term-care ombudsman.
constraints: The program advocates for residents; it does not replace emergency response, facility licensing or a private attorney.

name: Texas family caregiver support
organization: Texas Health and Human Services / Area Agencies on Aging
description: The aging network offers caregiver information, service referrals and respite information.
next_step: Ask your aging agency about caregiver support, training and respite options, and describe the care needs.
constraints: Ask which programs fit the caregiver and care recipient; eligibility and local service availability vary.

fields_supported: AAA and ADRC caregiver support routes

name: Texas Technology Access Program
description: Assistive technology demonstrations, device trials and reuse information.
next_step: Describe the task or access barrier and ask about a device demonstration, short-term loan or reuse referral.
constraints: Ask about available equipment, suitability and loan conditions. Some complex devices need a professional involved. A device referral does not promise installation or permanent equipment.

fields_supported: short-term loan process and professional involvement for some devices

name: Disability Rights Texas
description: State protection and advocacy intake for disability-related legal rights concerns.
next_step: Use the statewide intake line and describe the disability-related concern; ask whether the issue fits current services.
constraints: The organization reviews requests and cannot accept every case. Requests use the designated intake process, not email or direct staff calls.

fields_supported: state protection and advocacy organization identity

name: Independent Living Services for Older Individuals Who Are Blind
description: Independent living help for adults age 55 or older with significant vision impairment.
next_step: Call the OIB helpline and ask about assessment, daily living skills, orientation or mobility training and adaptive aids.
constraints: The program reviews individual needs and criteria. For employment goals or other ages, ask about the appropriate separate vision service.
Phone and age/scope are supported by Hockley County’s official resource guide; the TWC brochure corroborates the program helpline.

fields_supported: Older Individuals Who Are Blind program
source_evidence.published_or_revised_on: File labeled 2025; body publication date not stated

name: Relay Texas
organization: Relay Texas / Public Utility Commission of Texas
description: Telephone relay connects TTY users and people using standard voice phones.
next_step: Dial 711 or 800-735-2989 and give the operator the number you want to call; ask about the communication mode that fits your needs.
constraints: Ask about device or service requirements for other relay modes.

fields_supported: state university AT program identifies Relay Texas access numbers and PUC oversight

name: 2-1-1 Texas community resources
organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
description: State information and referral for local housing, food, utilities and other community resources.
next_step: Give your county and describe the help needed; ask for local intake contacts and how to apply.
constraints: A referral does not establish eligibility, available funding, an opening or a bed.

name: Families in Crisis, Inc.: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 12-TX-071): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Contact this provider through VA’s National Call Center for Homeless Veterans (877-424-3838) with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you.
constraints: Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies. Ask about current funding and availability. A referral is not an approval or housing reservation.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
